spec.description: Hive Desktop's own telemetry: process and Go runtime metrics, terminal streaming, source polling, logs, traces, and continuous profiles. Defined in grafana/ of the hive-desktop repository.
A steady sawtooth is healthy; a staircase that never comes down is a leak.
spec.title: Goroutines over time

spec.description: Every log line the app emits, bucketed by Loki's detected level. A step change in error or warn is the thing to notice.
spec.title: Log volume by level

spec.description: Count over the dashboard time range. Zero is healthy.
spec.title: Errors and warnings

spec.description: The lines behind the count. Structured fields the app logged ride along as Loki structured metadata.
spec.title: Errors and warnings, most recent first

spec.description: Unfiltered stream for the selected channel and build.
spec.title: All logs

spec.description: The Go runtime's own accounting, stacked so the top is its total. Summed across the selected builds; narrow Build for one.
spec.title: Memory in use by class

spec.description: Bytes allocated per second. Churn, not footprint -- a high rate with flat usage is fine.
spec.title: Allocation rate

spec.description: The latest traces for the selected channel and build. Click a Trace ID to open the span waterfall.
spec.title: Recent traces

options.content:
Trigger spans are the roots: **`app.startup`**, **`ingest.tick`**, **`terminal.attach`**, and one per dispatched action type. Waits hang below them: `ingest.source <kind>`, `http.<source> <method>`, `db.CommitBatch`, `tmux.*`, and `dispatch.*`.

**Open a trace:** click a **Trace ID** in the table for the span waterfall.

**Go further, scoped to the current Channel/Build:**

- [Traces Drilldown](/a/grafana-exploretraces-app/explore?var-ds=${traces}&var-filters=resource.service.name%7C%3D%7Chive-desktop&var-filters=resource.deployment.environment.name%7C%3D~%7C${environment:regex}&var-filters=resource.service.version%7C%3D~%7C${version:regex}) -- service-level breakdowns, no query needed
- [Profiles Drilldown](/a/grafana-pyroscope-app/explore?explorationType=flame-graph&var-dataSource=${profiles}&var-serviceName=hive-desktop&var-profileMetricId=process_cpu:cpu:nanoseconds:cpu:nanoseconds) -- flame graphs for any window, diffable between builds
- [Explore ▸ Tempo](/explore?left=%7B%22datasource%22:%22${traces}%22,%22queries%22:%5B%7B%22queryType%22:%22traceql%22,%22query%22:%22%7Bresource.service.name%3D%5C%22hive-desktop%5C%22%20%26%26%20resource.deployment.environment.name%3D~%5C%22${environment:regex}%5C%22%20%26%26%20resource.service.version%3D~%5C%22${version:regex}%5C%22%7D%22%7D%5D%7D) -- raw TraceQL against this service
- [Explore ▸ Loki](/explore?left=%7B%22datasource%22:%22${logs}%22,%22queries%22:%5B%7B%22expr%22:%22%7Bservice_name%3D%5C%22hive-desktop%5C%22,%20deployment_environment_name%3D~%5C%22${environment:regex}%5C%22%7D%20%7C%20service_version%3D~%5C%22${version:regex}%5C%22%22%7D%5D%7D) -- the log stream beside it

spec.description: Object count per second. Read beside allocation rate: many small objects look different from few large ones.
spec.title: Allocations per second

spec.description: app.startup spans in the range: one per app launch.
spec.title: Launches

spec.description: Spans that ended with an error status, at any depth.
spec.title: Error spans in range

spec.description: HTTP client spans with no parent. An HTTP call is a wait and belongs under a trigger span, so this should be zero; anything else is a code path that calls a provider outside a trigger.
spec.title: Untriggered HTTP spans

spec.description: Root spans by name: each is a distinct cause entering the app, such as a launch, a poll tick, or a terminal attach. Grafana Cloud renames HTTP client spans to the bare method; the original name is in span.grafana.original_span_name.
spec.title: Triggers per minute

spec.description: 95th percentile duration of each root span, on a log axis. Trace metrics cover at most 25 hours.
spec.title: Trigger duration p95

spec.description: Heap size that triggers the next GC cycle, last value in range. Memory in use crossing it starts a cycle.
spec.title: GC target

spec.expr: count by (deployment_environment_name, service_version, telemetry_sdk_version, host_id) (last_over_time(target_info{job="hive-desktop", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", service_version=~"$version"}[$__range]))

spec.description: One row per build that sent telemetry in the range. Launches counts service.instance.id values, which every launch mints fresh. A host_id column appears once telemetry.host_id is set.
spec.title: Build inventory

spec.description: Times tmux paused the stream because the broker fell behind. Zero is the healthy reading and the expected one: a pause means the backlog filled.
spec.title: Backlog pauses

spec.description: Bytes per second decoded from tmux %output and handed to the broker. A sustained plateau is a program painting continuously; a spike is an attach snapshot.
spec.title: Stream throughput

spec.description: Decode to websocket. p50 against p99 separates a uniformly slow stream from one with a bad tail: a p99 rising against a flat p50 is backpressure, not load.
spec.title: Frame latency percentiles

spec.description: Bytes queued in the broker when a frame was published, against an 8 MiB bound. A sustained climb is what precedes a pause and then the overflow resync.
spec.title: Broker backlog depth

spec.description: terminal.attach spans, from opening a terminal to its first paint. Each point is an interval with an attach in it, on a log axis. p95 pulling away from p50 is a slow tmux server, not a slow app. Trace metrics cover at most 25 hours.
spec.title: Attach duration

spec.description: Requests left in each provider's window, as of the last response that reported one. A source only appears once it has sent an X-RateLimit-Remaining header, so an absent line means the provider does not publish one.
spec.title: Rate limit headroom by source

spec.description: Outbound calls for each connector. Per minute rather than per second because a poll loop is spiky and fires on a minute-plus cadence: a per-second reading of the same data is a string of near-zero decimals.
spec.title: Requests per minute by source

spec.description: Anything that was not a 2xx or a 3xx, which deliberately includes calls that never got a status at all: a failed connection carries an error_type and no status code, and a filter on status alone would hide it.
spec.title: Failures per minute by source

spec.expr: 1 - (sum by (source) (rate(http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{job="hive-desktop", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", service_version=~"$version", source!="", http_response_status_code!="304"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (source) (rate(http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{job="hive-desktop", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", service_version=~"$version", source!=""}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.description: Share of responses that were 304 Not Modified. This is what makes polling cheap: an authenticated 304 costs no rate-limit budget, so a high ratio is healthy and a fall means the app started paying for data it already had. Written as 1 minus the non-304 share so a source with no 304s yet reads 0 rather than dropping out of the query.
spec.title: Conditional hit ratio by source

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, source) (rate(http_client_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="hive-desktop", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", service_version=~"$version", source!=""}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.description: 95th percentile round trip per connector, measured at the transport, so it includes redirects and TLS.
spec.title: Request duration p95 by source

spec.description: ingest.tick spans: one poll of every due source, on a log axis. A slow tick is what makes a feed look stale. Trace metrics cover at most 25 hours.
spec.title: Poll tick duration

spec.description: ingest.source spans, one per source per tick, on a log axis. The slowest kind is what holds a tick open. Trace metrics cover at most 25 hours.
spec.title: Drain duration p95 by source kind

spec.description: Feed fetches per interval. not_modified should dominate a healthy feed; unreachable, http_error, too_large, and parse_failure say whether a failure is the network, the server, or the document. Empty until an RSS source runs.
spec.title: RSS fetches by outcome

spec.description: Processor limit. A constant, so it is a number rather than a graph.
spec.title: GOMAXPROCS

spec.description: Percent of one logical core, so a busy process can pass 100. self is the app's own process; descendants is every process below it: tmux, shells, and agents. Climbing descendants with a flat self line is a terminal program, not Hive.
spec.title: CPU

spec.description: Cores the profiler saw the app's own process use. Drag across a spike to narrow the flame graphs below to that window.
spec.title: Profiled CPU

spec.description: Where the app's own process spends CPU, merged across the selected builds and time range. Child processes are not profiled.
spec.title: CPU by function

spec.description: Read the proportions, not the sizes: the graph merges every heap snapshot in the range, so its total is a sum of snapshots. The profiler does not force a GC, so garbage the next cycle frees can show here.
spec.title: Heap in use by allocation site

spec.description: Every byte allocated in the range: churn, not footprint. This is what drives Allocation rate on the Runtime tab and the GC work behind it.
spec.title: Allocated bytes by allocation site

spec.description: Memory the OS holds for each scope, the number Activity Monitor shows. It includes what the Go runtime does not manage, so it sits above Memory in use by class.
spec.title: Resident memory

spec.description: Processes below the app. The walk stops at 64, and a red line at the cap marks a sample where it did: the CPU and memory descendants lines are then a floor, not the whole tree.
spec.title: Child processes
